messages:
alex: heads up — our onprem net-agent 1.3 rollout triggered a weird path: sidecars without hostNetwork still had outbound reachability to metadata IPs via the CNI eBPF hook. secops-bot posted a high sev alert.
secops-bot: [ALERT] 2024-04-15T09:02:10Z net-agent-1.3: unexpected egress to 169.254.169.254 from pod=redwood/ingest-sidecar-abc123
maya: omg. reproduction steps?
devon: repro: deploy simple pod with sidecar, hostNetwork: false, attach net-agent 1.3. From sidecar: curl http://169.254.169.254/ -> 200. Host network not set on pod.
jen: that smells like the CNI hook bypassing netpols via eBPF shim. We should confirm netpol enforcement point (node vs pod). Any kernel logs?
devon: kernel dmesg shows nftables drop rules applied but eBPF program returned redirect to host stack. snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] cni-ebpf: redirect IF_INDEX=2 proto=6 dst=169.254.169.254
```
maya: ok so mitigation options: 1) block metadata at node level (iptables/nft on host), 2) eBPF policy to deny host-facing redirects, 3) change RBAC/serviceaccount restrictions for the agent to remove CAP_NET_ADMIN where possible.
priya: also need to consider audit logging and KMS access for private deploys — if sidecar can hit metadata it could exfiltrate IMDS creds used for KMS unwrap. We must ensure envelope keys never rely on IMDS tokens in private deployments.
sam: agreed. Incident triage: I filed INF-4821 (priv-deploy metadata egress). CVE candidate being evaluated. Short-term: add node-level blocklist for 169.254.169.254 and 169.254.170.2 plus deny routes in host netns.
alex: proposed short plan
- emergency node-level block (iptables/nft) for metadata IPs (hotfix)
- update net-agent to remove redirect path + disable that eBPF program
- add admission webhook check that denies pod annotations that request the problematic feature
- RBAC: remove privileged SA binding used by net-agent in private deployments; require explicit opt-in with ticket
- audit: forward net-agent ACL events to customer SIEM over TLS and to our internal splunk index (rsyslog TLS)
jen: can you paste the nft rule we want to push via user-data/terraform for private nodes? I can PR to infra.
devon: sample nft rule:
```
table inet redwood-block {
  chain prerouting {
    type filter hook prerouting priority 0;
    ip daddr 169.254.169.254 drop
    ip daddr 169.254.170.2 drop
  }
}
```
maya: +1. Also for k8s netpol fallback add explicit egress deny in default namespace as conservative guard.
priya: KMS integration note: for Private deployments we enforce HSM/KMS unwrap via a short-lived envelope key that is provisioned via PV with restricted mount. Do not fetch KMS credentials from IMDS; use customer KMS endpoint inside VPC and mutual TLS.
sam: will update runbook: IR playbook steps include isolate node, snapshot net-agent config, rotate any keys that may have been used, run yara scan for exfil tools.
alex: audit logging config (example rsyslog forward):
```
# /etc/rsyslog.d/50-netagent.conf
module(load="imfile")
input(type="imfile" File="/var/log/net-agent/audit.log" Tag="net-agent" Severity="info")
action(type="omfwd" Target="siem.collector.internal" Port="6514" Protocol="tcp" StreamDriver="gtls" StreamDriverMode="1")
```
devon: can we do a canary on Dedicated/GCP first then push to onprem? we should roll to a small set of private nodes.
jen: yes — create a canary node pool and enable blocklist there first.
maya: also update our netpol catalog docs to call out eBPF shims as enforcement gaps and recommended host-level blocklists.
priya: one last thing — policy for service accounts: new minimum permissions for net-agent in private deployments: no cluster-admin, no hostPID, no hostNetwork, drop CAP_NET_ADMIN. Documented and enforced by OPA gate.
alex: action items:
- devon: push nft/iptables hotfix to infra canary (ETA 2h) 
- jen: create INF-4821 triage channel and runbook edits (ETA 1h)
- priya: update KMS/HSM guidance + mandatory mTLS note (ETA EOD)
- maya: docs + netpol catalog update (ETA tomorrow)
- sam: IR checklist and key-rotation play (ETA 3h)
I'll slack infra and ops-collector to start canary. :thumbsup:
secops-bot: INF-4821 created and assigned: sam, devon, priya — severity=high
alex: thanks — keep this thread updated with canary results and logs. If anyone finds evidence of token exfiltration, we escalate immediate key rotation.
